title: Cyclotomic Extensions
---

:::definition{17.10.1} Cyclotomic extension
The $n$th cyclotomic extension of ${\QQ}$ is ${\QQ}(\zeta_n)$ where $\zeta_n = e^{2\pi i/n}$ is a primitive $n$th root of unity. The minimal polynomial of $\zeta_n$ over ${\QQ}$ is the $n$th cyclotomic polynomial $\Phi_n(x)$, which has degree $\varphi(n)$ (Euler’s totient).
:::

:::proposition{17.10.1} Galois group of cyclotomic extensions
The extension ${\QQ}(\zeta_n)/{\QQ}$ is Galois, and $$\Gal({\QQ}(\zeta_n)/{\QQ}) \cong ({\ZZ}/n)^\times.$$ The isomorphism sends $\sigma_a$ (defined by $\sigma_a(\zeta_n) = \zeta_n^a$) to $a \bmod n$.
:::

:::note
This is abelian, so every subextension of ${\QQ}(\zeta_n)/{\QQ}$ is Galois over ${\QQ}$. The Kronecker–Weber theorem states that *every* abelian extension of ${\QQ}$ is contained in some cyclotomic extension.
:::
